phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Open-system programming is framed as a fixed processor receiving a time-dependent program state π_t to reproduce e^{tL} on arbitrary input states.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Architecture-level diagram for the programmable Lindbladian processor.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, paragraph ending with theorem statement near line 109
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Any fully dissipative n-qubit Lindbladian whose jump operators are all Pauli operators is quantum programmable.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Constructive programmability claim for fully dissipative Pauli Lindbladians.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Any UU-covariant Lindbladian is quantum programmable with finite program dimension determined by the commutant structure of \bar U⊗U.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Covariant-semigroup programmability corollary and its program-dimension rule.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, necessary-condition paragraph and Appendix proposition label prop:sufficient_cond_cptp
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: A quantum-programmable Lindbladian must admit a representation L(ρ)=α(E(ρ)−ρ) for some quantum channel E and α≥0.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Necessary structural condition for exact quantum programmability.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Proposition on coherent generators
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Any Lindbladian with a nontrivial coherent part H \not\propto I_d is not quantum programmable.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: No-go proposition for coherent Lindbladian generators.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Proposition on spontaneous emission
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The qubit amplitude-damping Lindbladian generated by L=√γ|0⟩⟨1| is not quantum programmable.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: No-go proposition for the amplitude-damping Lindbladian.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: For a purely coherent Lindbladian i ad_H with K distinct eigenvalues, there exists an exact quasi-sampling programming protocol using program states of dimension K.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Constructive HPTP-programming protocol for coherent dynamics.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The amplitude-damping Lindbladian admits an exact quasi-sampling programming protocol with program-state dimension 12.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Constructive HPTP-programming protocol for amplitude damping.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Fig. 2 and surrounding paragraph
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: For the SWAP-dephasing Lindbladian with λ=0.5, the quasi-sampled dynamics closely match the exact overlap formula (1+e^{-λt}cos 2t)/2 over t∈[0,10].
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Numerical time-evolution comparison between quasi-sampling estimates and the exact SWAP-dephasing solution.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The ε-error programming cost γ_ε(π_t,L,T) is the binary logarithm of the minimum diamond norm of a retrieval map that approximates e^{tL} for all t in [0,T].

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, property list under programming cost
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: For analytic program states, the exact programming cost obeys analytic continuation γ(π_t,L)=γ(π_t,L,T) for every T>0.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Analytic-continuation property of the exact programming cost.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, property list under programming cost
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The exact programming cost is faithful: γ(π_t,L)≥0 and equals zero exactly when L is CPTP-programmable.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Faithfulness property of the programming-cost measure.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, property list under programming cost
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Applying invertible noise N to the program states increases the cost within the bounds γ(π_t,L)≤γ(N(π_t),L)≤γ(π_t,L)+log||N^{-1}||_⋄.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Fig. 3 and accompanying paragraph

phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Numerically estimated cost-versus-error curves for two Lindbladian families.
